name: Zygomatic arch reduction / reduction malarplasty
lead: Reduction malarplasty is a facial-bone surgery that narrows a wide or prominent cheekbone (zygoma) by cutting and repositioning the malar complex or zygomatic arch.[1][4] Published authors describe it as one of the more commonly requested facial-contour procedures in East Asia and as rarely performed in the West.[1][3]

Techniques have evolved from coronal-incision approaches, which leave a scalp scar and carry facial-nerve risk, toward intraoral and limited-incision osteotomies.[2][3] The literature is made up of surgeon case series and technique descriptions; randomized trials were not found.

In looksmaxxing forums the term ZSO (zygomatic skeletal osteotomy) appears mostly in discussions about the opposite aim, projecting or repositioning cheekbones, and posters often compare it with malar implants and midface advancement.[7]

paras: An early technique used a coronal incision and either transposition osteoplasty of the malar complex or its removal and refixation.[1] Later authors described intraoral approaches intended to avoid visible scars, facial-nerve injury and long operative times.[2][4] A retrospective study of 418 cases reported an L-shaped osteotomy through an intraoral approach intended to allow control of the degree of reduction.[3] A percutaneous approach using small 3-mm incisions has also been described.[6]

Zygomatic nonunion, in which the cut bone fails to heal, has been reported as a complication in the literature.[5] The authors of intraoral and limited-incision methods cite scars and facial-nerve injury as drawbacks of coronal approaches.[2]
Published human studies are retrospective surgical case series and technique reports, including a 418-case series from 2009.[3] No randomized controlled trials were found among the sources reviewed.

A looksmax.org thread shows a user asking whether a ZSO or malarplasty with autologous bone would help the eye area, and a reply attributing flat cheekbones to a recessed maxilla and suggesting a LeFort III osteotomy instead.[7] This reflects a common forum framing in which cheek appearance is linked to midface projection.

timeline.event: Description of reduction malarplasty by coronal approach with osteoplasty.[1]
Methods developed to avoid the larger coronal incision.[4]
L-shaped intraoral osteotomy reported in 418 cases.[3]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org the ZSO is discussed within the broader topic of cheekbone and midface surgery.[7]

claims.claim: Flat cheekbones are really a recessed maxilla problem rather than a cheek problem
claims.believers: One poster replied that the cheeks look flat because the maxilla is not projected and suggested a LeFort III osteotomy to bring the midface forward.[7]
claims.experts: The sources reviewed describe malarplasty as a procedure to reduce prominent zygomas, and do not address this claim.[1][3]

card.summary: Cheekbone-narrowing osteotomy, mainly an East Asian aesthetic surgery, supported only by surgeon case series.
card.note: Major bone surgery with nerve injury and nonunion reported.

quick.overview:
Reduction malarplasty cuts and repositions the cheekbone to narrow a wide or prominent midface. Surgeons describe it as a commonly requested contouring procedure in East Asia.

The published literature is mostly retrospective case series and technique papers.
quick.mechanism: Osteotomies are made in the malar complex or zygomatic arch, through coronal, intraoral, preauricular or small percutaneous incisions, and the bone is repositioned or fixed.
quick.risks: Reported concerns include scars and facial-nerve injury with some approaches, and zygomatic nonunion after surgery. It is major surgery performed by trained surgeons.
